name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: name
description: Specify a name for the document template to be created.

name: content
description: A form field that drivers must complete when executing a route step. Defines the data structure and validation rules for collecting required information during route execution.

name: content[].label
description: Specify the label or the name of the field. The `label` specified here can be used as field name when rendering the document in the Driver app.

name: content[].name
description: Specify the name of the document field. A field's`name` can be used for internal references to the document field.

name: content[].type
description: Specify the data type of the field. It corresponds to the type of information that the driver needs to collect.

name: content[].required
description: Specify if it is mandatory to fill the field. Default value is false.

name: content[].validation
description: Specify the validation rules for the field. This can be used to enforce data quality and integrity checks. For example, if the field is a number type, `validation` can define constraints like minimum / maximum number values.

name: content[].validation.min
description: Specifies the minimum allowed value for `number` type document field. Input values must be greater than or equal to this threshold.

name: content[].validation.max
description: Specifies the maximum allowed value for `number` type document field. Input values must be less than or equal to this threshold.

name: content[].validation.min_items
description: Specifies the minimum number of items for `multi_choices`, `photos` type document fields. The number of provided input items must be greater than or equal to this threshold.

name: content[].validation.max_items
description: Specifies the maximum number of items for `multi_choices`, `photos` type document fields. The number of provided input items must be less than or equal to this threshold.

name: content[].meta
description: An object to define additional information required for `single_choice` or `multi_choices` type document items.

name: content[].meta.options
description: An array of objects to define options for a `multi_choices` or `single_choice` type document field. Each object represents one option.

name: content[].meta.options[].label
description: Specify the label or name for the option.

name: content[].meta.options[].value
description: Specify the value associated with the option. This value will be submitted when the option is checked in the Driver app.

name: driver_email
description: Specify the e-mail address of the driver who should receive the route. The e-mail address must be registered in [NextBillion.ai Cloud Console](https://console.nextbillion.ai/).

name: steps
description: An array of objects to collect the details about the intermediate steps in the route to be dispatched. Each object corresponds to a single step. The array must begin with a start-type step and end with an end-type step, to form a valid route.

name: steps[].type
description: Specify the step type. It can belong to one of the following: `start`, `job` , `pickup`, `delivery`, `end`. A `duration` is mandatory when the step type is either `layover` or a `break`.

name: steps[].arrival
description: Specify the scheduled arrival time of the driver, as an UNIX timestamp in seconds, at the step. Please note that: * Arrival time for each step should be equal to or greater than the previous step. * Past times can not be provided. * The time provided is used only for informative display on the driver app and it does not impact or get affected by the route generated.

name: steps[].location
description: Specify the location coordinates where the steps should be performed in `[latitude, longitude]`.

name: steps[].address
description: Specify the postal address for the step.

name: steps[].meta
description: An object to specify any additional details about the task to be associated with the step in the response. The information provided here will be available on the Driver's app under step details. This attribute can be used to provide context about or instructions to the driver for performing the task

name: steps[].meta.customer_name
description: Specify the name of the customer for which the step has to be performed.

name: steps[].meta.customer_phone_number
description: Specify the phone number of the person to be contacted when at step location.

name: steps[].meta.instructions
description: Specify custom instructions to be carried out while performing the step.

name: steps[].document_template_id
description: Specify the ID of the document template to be used for collecting proof of completion for the step. If not specified, the document template specified at the route level will be used for the step. Use the [Documents API](https://docs.nextbillion.ai/docs/dispatches/documents-api) to create, read and manage the document templates. Please note that the document template ID can not be assigned to following step types - `start`, `end`, `break`, `layover`.

name: steps[].duration
description: Specify the duration of the `layover` or `break` type steps, in seconds. Please note it is mandatory when step type is either "layover" or "break".

name: steps[].completion_mode
description: Specify the mode of completion to be used for the step. Currently, following values are allowed: * `manual`: Steps must be marked as completed manually through the Driver App. * `geofence`: Steps are marked as completed automatically based on the entry conditions and geofence specified. * `geofence_manual_fallback`: Steps will be marked as completed automatically based on geofence and entry condition configurations but there will also be a provision for manually updating the status in case, geofence detection fails.

name: steps[].geofence_config
description: Specify the configurations of the geofence which will be used to detect presence of the driver and complete the tasks automatically. Please note that this attribute is required when `completion_mode` is either "geofence" or "geofence_manual_fallback".

name: steps[].geofence_config.type
description: Specify the type of the geofence. Currently, `circle` is the only suppoeted value.

name: steps[].geofence_config.radius
description: Specify the radius of the cicular geofence, in meters. Once specified, the service will create a geofence with task's location as the center of the circle having the given radius. Valid values for `radius` are \[10, 5000\].

name: routing
description: The `routing` object allows defining the routing characteristics that should be used to generate a route when the Driver uses the in-app navigation. Only `car` mode is supported currently.

name: routing.mode
description: Specify the driving mode that the service should use to determine a route

name: routing.avoid
description: Setting this will ensure the generated route avoids the object(s) specified in the input. Multiple values should be separated by a pipe (|). If `none` is provided along with other values, an error is returned as a valid route is not feasible.

name: routing.truck_size
description: Specify the dimensions of a truck, in centimeters (cm), in the format of <height, width, length>. When specified, the dispatched route uses only those roads which allow trucks with specified dimensions. Please note this parameter is effective only when `mode=truck`. Also, the maximum dimensions that can be specified are as follows: Height = 1000 cm Width = 5000 cm Length = 5000 cm

name: routing.truck_weight
description: Specify the weight of the truck, including trailers and shipped goods, in kilograms (kg). When specified, the dispatched route uses only those roads which allow trucks with specified weight. Please note this parameter is effective only when `mode=truck`. Also, the maximum weight that can be specified for a truck is 100,000 kgs.

name: routing.truck_axle_load
description: Specify the total load per axle (including the weight of trailers and shipped goods) of the truck, in tonnes. When specified, the dispatched route uses only those roads which can be used by a truck to carry the specified load per axle. Please note this parameter is effective only when `mode=truck`.

name: routing.hazmat_type
description: Specify the type of hazardous material being carried and the dispatch service will avoid roads which are not suitable for the type of goods specified. Multiple values can be separated using a pipe operator `|` . Please note that this parameter is effective only when `mode=truck`.

name: distance
description: Specify the total distance, in meters, for an informative display in Driver's app. The distance specified here has no effect on the actual route that the service generates.

name: document_template_id
description: Specify the ID of the document template that should be used to collect proof of completion for all steps in the route. In order to complete each route step, the driver will need to submit a form generated by the rules defined in the given document template. Use the [Documents API](https://docs.nextbillion.ai/docs/dispatches/documents-api) to create, read and manage document templates. Please note that the document template ID assigned to a route does not apply to following step types - `start`, `end`, `break`, `layover`.

name: ro_request_id
description: Specify the Route Optimization request ID. When this ID is provided, all other fields will be ignored (including the required fields) and the route optimization result will be used to form the routes and corresponding steps. Please note that: * The driver's email ID must be provided in input `vehicle.metadata` as `user_email` such that the route optimization result must contain a valid driver email, step's arrival time, etc., to make a successful dispatch. * Document Template for collecting proof of delivery or completion can not be specified when using this field to dispatch a route. * In case of an error at any part among the routes, the API will immediately return the error with the index of the specific route or route step. * On a successful dispatch, the API returns the last route, if there are many, in the response payload.

name: routeID
description: Provide the ID of a previously dispatched route which needs to be modified. Both the `id` and `short_id` of the route are a valid input.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: operations
description: A collection of objects with details of the steps to be modified. Each object corresponds to a single step.

name: operations[].operation
description: Specify the type of operation to be performed for the step.

name: operations[].data.step_id
description: Specify the ID of the step to be updated or deleted. Either one of `id` or `short_id` of the step can be provided. This input will be ignored when `operation: create` .

name: distance
description: Specify the distance of the route.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: type
description: Indicate the type of area to retrieve the road segments it contains. Only a "circle" or a "bbox" can be specified.

name: circle
description: An object to collect the details of a circular area. Please note that `circle` attribute is effective only when `type = circle`.

name: circle.center
description: Specify the coordinates of the center of the circular area.

name: circle.center.lat
description: Latitude of the circle's center location.

name: circle.center.lon
description: Longitude of the circle's center location.

name: circle.radius
description: Specify the radius of the circle, in meters, of the circular area.

name: bbox
description: An object to collect details of a bounding box's boundaries. Please note that `bbox` attribute is effective only when `type = bbox`.

name: bbox.max_lat
description: Specify the maximum latitude of the bounding box area.

name: bbox.max_lon
description: Specify the maximum longitude of the bounding box area.

name: bbox.min_lat
description: Specify the minimum latitude of the bounding box area.

name: bbox.min_lon
description: Specify the minimum longitude of the bounding box area.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: bbox
description: Specify the bounding box indicating the area to be used for retrieving the incidents from. The bouding box can be specified using a pair of location coordinates - first pair is for the lower-left corner of the bounding box and the second pair for the upper-right corner of the box. Please note that * Maximum area of the specified bounding box is 10,000 km2. * One of `bbox` and `id` is mandatory. * However, when both `id` and `bbox` are provided, the `bbox` input is ignored.

name: id
description: Provide a comma separated list of specific incident's IDs to be retrieved. The maximum number of IDs that can be provided in a list is 5. Users need to provide at least one of `bbox` and `id` for a valid input request. Please note when both `id` and `bbox` are provided in the input request, the `bbox` input is ignored. **Note:** Incidents IDs can be retrieved from results of previous queries with the 'bbox' parameter.

name: incident_type
description: Specify the types of incidents incidents to be included in the response. Multiple values are supported and should be separated by a comma `,`.

name: incident_validity
description: Specify the choice of incidents based on their occurrence in time. Multiple values can be separated by a comma `,`.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: region
description: Specifies the region for which the weather polygons are to be fetched. Allowed value details: `europe`: Europe; `nam`: North America; `usa`: United States of America; `australia`: Australia; `latam`: Latin Americas.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: at
description: The coordinates of the location for which the forecast is requested, formatted as `lat,lon`. Latitude must be in the range `-90` to `90` and longitude in the range `-180` to `180`.

name: forecastHours
description: The number of hours of forecast data to return, starting from the current hour. The accepted range is `1` to `24`.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: at
description: The coordinates of the location for which the forecast is requested, formatted as `lat,lon`. Latitude must be in the range `-90` to `90` and longitude in the range `-180` to `180`.

name: forecastDays
description: The number of days of forecast data to return, starting from the current day in the station's local time. The accepted range is `1` to `14`.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to an API.

name: mapId
description: Identifier of the maps. Please check with NextBillion at [support@nextbillion.ai](mailto:support@nextbillion.ai) for any other custom values for your key.

name: tileSize
description: Specify the tileSize. Only 256 is the accepted value.

name: z
description: Specifies the tile's zoom level. You can use between 0 to 22 as zoom levels.

name: x
description: Specifies the tile's column. Please note that only the values less than 2^z are valid for this parameter.

name: y
description: Specifies the tile's row. Please note that only the values less than 2^z are valid for this parameter.

name: scale
description: Use “@2x” to get “retina”/HiDPI image.

name: format
description: The format of the tile image to be returned in the response. NextBillion supports `jpg` format by default. In order to get `png` and `webp` formats, pleaser reach out at [support@nextbillion.ai](mailto:support@nextbillion.ai) to know more.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: path
description: Define path(s) to be drawn on top of the map. The polyline co-ordinates should be in (latitude,longitude) order. Use pipe (`|`) to separate the coordinates and other properties of the path. Available properties for the `path` parameter are: * `fill` - Color to use as the fill (e.g. `red`, `rgba(255,255,255,0.5)`, `#0000ff`, `none`, `false`) * `stroke` - The color of the `path` stroke `width` - Width of the `stroke` (in pixels) * `enc` - Encoded path geometry in the [Google Encoded Polyline Format](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/utilities/polylinealgorithm). If used, the rest of the path parameter is considered to be part of the encoded polyline string. Consequently, users need not specify the coordinate pairs. This parameter can be be used multiple times. You can also use `fill`, `stroke` and `width` as separate query parameters to specify default styling for all the paths.

name: markers
description: Define marker(s) to be drawn on top of the map. Can be used multiple times. Each marker is a comma-separated [longitude,latitude] pair. Individual markers are separated with a pipe symbol (`|`). Each marker can also have a different color - specified as the 3rd parameter. Additionally, the following special "commands" can be used (in the form of `key:value` appended before the `marker` coordinates): * `icon` - URL to a remote image (URL-encoded). You can use a URL shortener service to create more compact queries. The icon has to be at most 64 kB and 4096 pixels (e.g., 64x64 image). If used, the specified colors of the markers are ignored. * `anchor` - The anchor point of the custom icon. Allowed values are `top`, `left`, `bottom`, `right`, `center`, `topleft`, `bottomleft`, `topright`, `bottomright` with `bottom` being the default value. * `scale` - the scale of the image (useful if you want to provide a HiDPI image that scales down correctly), the default value is 1.

name: attribution
description: Changes the position of map attribution. If you disable the attribution make sure to display it in your application yourself (visibly).

name: mapId
description: Identifier of the map.

name: lat
description: Latitude of the point at the center of the image.

name: lon
description: Latitude of the point at the center of the image.

name: zoom
description: Zoom level of the resulting image (can be fractional). (In the tile pyramid based on 512x512 tiles.)

name: width
description: Width of the image in pixels.

name: height
description: Height of the image in pixels.

name: scale
description: Use `@2x` to get "retina"/HiDPI image.

name: format
description: The value depends on the Map settings.

description: Specifies the tile's zoom level. You can use values between 0 to 15 as zoom levels.

name: x
description: Specifies the tile's column. The maximum value is 2<sup>z</sup>.

name: y
description: Specifies the tile's row. The maximum value is 2<sup>z</sup>.

name: format
description: Specifies the format of the tiles to be returned.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: description
description: Set a custom `description` for the clustering problem.

name: options
description: An object to configure the `routing` options, cost `objective` and `constraint` parameters enabling users to emulate their clustering requirements.

name: options.routing
description: An object for users to customize the routing options for their clustering requirements. Users can define the rules like `mode`, `departure_time`, `truck_size`, and `truck_weight` using this object.

name: options.routing.mode
description: Set the driving mode which would be used to determine the cost of clustering the given jobs/locations. The cost type can be configured using the `travel_cost` parameter under the `routing` object. Please note that setting `mode:air` implies straight line travel between locations.

name: options.routing.option
description: Use this option to make use of truck dimension parameters like `truck_weight` or `truck size` or switch to time based routing.

name: options.routing.departure_time
description: A UNIX epoch timestamp in seconds format that is used to set the departure time. The API will consider the typical traffic conditions at the given time to calculate the routing cost. If no input is provided, then the traffic conditions at the time of making the request are considered. Please note that this parameter is effective only when the `option=flexible`.

name: options.routing.truck_size
description: This defines the dimensions of a truck in centimeters (cm). Describe the parameters in the format `height,width,length`. This parameter is effective only when the `mode=truck` and `option=flexible`. Maximum dimensions are as follows: Height = 1000 cm Width = 1000 cm Length = 5000 cm

name: options.routing.truck_weight
description: This parameter defines the weight of the truck including trailers and shipped goods in kilograms. This parameter is effective only when `mode=truck` and `option=flexible`. Maximum allowed weight is 100000 kg (100 tonnes).

name: options.routing.approaches
description: Specify the side of the road from which to approach a given location while identifying the cost of a cluster. The approach configuration impacts the route to be taken and hence affects the distance / duration cost of the cluster as well. The acceptable values are "curb" and "unrestricted". If provided, the number of input strings in `approaches` must be equal to the number of locations provided. Multiple approach values should be separated by a `;` (semi-colon). However, you can skip a coordinate and show its position in the list using `;` (semi-colon). Please note these values are case-sensitive.

name: options.routing.hazmat_type
description: Specify the type of hazardous material being carried and the service will avoid roads which are not suitable for the type of goods specified. Provide multiple values separated by a pipe `|` . Please note that this parameter is effective only when `mode=truck` and `option=flexible` .

name: options.routing.avoid
description: Specify the type of objects/maneuvers that the service should avoid when identifying possible routes in a cluster. Use a pipe `|` to add multiple objects. If `none` is provided along with other values, an error is returned as a valid route is not feasible. The values are case sensitive.

name: options.routing.traffic_timestamp
description: Specify the general time when the jobs need to be carried out. The time should be expressed as an UNIX timestamp in seconds format. The service will take into account the general traffic conditions at the given time to determine the possible clusters and their costs.

name: options.objective
description: This enables users to customize the cost objective for their clustering requirements.

name: options.objective.travel_cost
description: This is used for specifying the type of cost associated with travel. The `travel_cost` parameter provides the API response with the unit which was used to estimate the cost, depending on the value provided. - If the value is set to `distance`, the API will minimize the total distance travelled (in meters) while moving from `job` locations to the cluster center. - If the value is set to `duration`, the API will minimize the total time taken (in seconds) to travel from `job` locations to the cluster center. - If the value is set to `air_distance`, the API will minimize the total straight line distance (in meters) from `job` locations to the cluster center.

name: options.constraint
description: An object to configure the cluster constraints. Please note that when the service is tasked with creating clusters automatically (i.e. when `clusters` attribute is not used), it will not create clusters containing less than 2 jobs. If needed, please use the `min_quantity` property of `clusters` attribute to override this constraint.

name: options.constraint.hard_quantity_constraint
description: By default, the service will always assign all the jobs. When `hard_quantity_constraint` is `true`, it will strictly adhere to the `min_quantity` and `max_quantity` constraints configured in the `clusters` object. Please note that: - when the sum of `quantity` of all `jobs` is less than the sum of `min_quantity` of all `clusters`, an error message is returned as no feasible solution is possible. - `jobs` will not be added to a cluster if its `quantity` causes the total quantity assigned to that cluster to exceed the `max_quantity`.

name: options.constraint.max_cluster_radius
description: A positive number denoting the maximum travelling cost that can be incurred when travelling from cluster’s center to any of its jobs . The travelling cost is determined using the metric specified in `travel_cost` parameter of `objective` property. * If the `travel_cost` is `distance` then, the `max_cluster_radius` is the maximum distance, in meters, allowed while travelling from the cluster’s center to any of its jobs. * If the `travel_cost` is `duration` then, the `max_cluster_radius` is the maximum duration, in seconds, allowed while travelling from the cluster’s center to any of its jobs. * If the `travel_cost` is `air_distance` then, the `max_cluster_radius` is the maximum straight line distance, in meters, allowed while travelling from the cluster’s center to any of its jobs. Please note that `max_cluster_radius` is mandatory when the `clusters` attribute is not provided. It is ineffective when `clusters` attribute is provided. This property is useful when users do not want to specify or are not sure of the properties of clusters to be created. In such cases, they can skip mentioning `clusters` object in the input and the service will create the required clusters automatically as per the given constraints.

name: options.constraint.max_cluster_quantity
description: Specify the maximum `quantity` (configured for each of the `jobs`) that can be assigned to a cluster. This is effective only when the `clusters` attribute is not provided. Please note that when `hard_quantity_constraint` is true, jobs causing violation of `max_cluster_quantity` will remain unassigned. This property is useful when users do not want to specify or are not sure of the properties of clusters to be created. In such cases, they can skip mentioning `clusters` object in the input and the service will create the required clusters automatically as per the given constraints.

name: clusters[].id
description: A non-zero, positive integer denoting the unique ID of the `cluster`. An error occurs if the same IDs for different clusters are provided. The `id` field is mandatory when using the `clusters` attribute.

name: clusters[].max_quantity
description: A positive integer to decide the maximum `quantity` that can be assigned to the `cluster`. Some `jobs` would remain unassigned if the sum of quantities of all the `jobs` exceeds the sum of `max_quantity` of all clusters. If not specified, we would assume it to be highest possible integer value i.e. 2147483647 is assumed to be the default `max_quantity`. Please note this is a soft constraint, unless `hard_quantity_constraint` property of the `constraint` attribute is `true`, in which case the API will strictly adhere to this constraint.

name: clusters[].min_quantity
description: A positive integer to decide the minimum `quantity` that can be assigned to the `cluster`. If the sum of `min_quantity` of all clusters is greater than the sum of the quantities of all the `jobs`, an error message is returned as no feasible solution is possible. If not specified, a default `min_quantity` of 0 is assumed. Please note this is a soft constraint, unless `hard_quantity_constraint` property of the `constraint` attribute is `true`, in which case, the API will strictly adhere to this constraint.

name: clusters[].center_location_index
description: A positive integer denoting the location index of the cluster’s center. If not specified, it leaves the algorithm to determine the cluster's center from the output. If the location index exceeds the count of input `locations`, the API will report an error.

name: clusters[].description
description: Set a custom description for the `cluster`.

name: clusters[].max_travel_cost
description: A positive integer specifying the maximum travel cost that can be incurred when travelling to a `job` location in the cluster from its center. The unit of this parameter is determined by the input of `travel_cost` parameter. - If `travel_cost` is set to `duration` then `max_travel_cost` is considered as maximum duration (in seconds) that is allowed to travel from the center of cluster to a `job` location. - If `travel_cost` is set to `distance` then `max_travel_cost` is considered as maximum distance (in meters) that is allowed to travel from the center of cluster to a `job` location. Please note that whenever `max_travel_cost` is specified for a cluster, then `min_quantity` for the cluster will always be considered as 0. Also, `max_travel_cost` is effective only when `hard_quantity_constraint` is false, otherwise an error is thrown.

name: jobs[].id
description: Provide an unique ID for the job. Please note `id` is mandatory when using the `jobs` object. The IDs are case-sensitive. **Note:** We have modified the data type of this field. However, the latest change is backward compatible and an integer type job ID is also valid.

name: jobs[].location_index
description: A positive integer denoting the location index of the `job`. If the location index exceeds the count of input locations, the API will report an error.

name: jobs[].quantity
description: The quantity associated with each `job`. It is typically a measure of workload or potential sales.

name: jobs[].description
description: Set a custom description for the `job`.

name: locations
description: An array of location coordinates in \[latitude,longitude\] format indicating all the geographical locations involved in the clustering problem. A maximum of 1000 locations can be added to this object. However, when using `options.objective.travel_cost:air_distance`: * Up to 4,000 locations are supported * Up to 20,000 locations are supported if `max_cluster_radius` is provided.

name: id
description: Unique task ID generated when the clustering POST request was submitted.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: key
description: A key is a unique identifier that is required to authenticate a request to the API.

name: orders
description: Collects the details of open orders to be fulfilled. Each object represents one order. All requests must include `orders` as a mandatory input. A maximum of 200 orders is allowed per request.

name: orders[].id
description: Specify a unique ID for the order.

name: orders[].pickup
description: Specify the location coordinates of the pickup location of the order. This input is mandatory for each order.

name: orders[].pickup.lat
description: Latitude of the pickup location.

name: orders[].pickup.lng
description: Longitude of the pickup location.

name: orders[].dropoffs
description: Use this parameter to specify the location coordinates of the destination of the trip or the intermediate stops to be completed before it. Please note * The last location provided is treated as the destination of the trip. * `dropoffs` is mandatory when `dropoff_details` is set to **true**.

name: orders[].dropoffs[].lat
description: Latitude of the stop location.

name: orders[].dropoffs[].lng
description: Longitude of the stop location.

name: orders[].service_time
description: Specify the service time, in seconds, for the order. Service time is the duration that the driver is likely to wait at the pickup location after arriving. The impact of the service time is realized in the ETA for the "dropoff" type step.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences
description: Define custom preferences for task assignment based on vehicle's attributes. If multiple criteria are provided, they are evaluated using an AND condition—meaning all specified criteria must be met individually for a vehicle to be considered. For example, if `required_all_of_attributes`, `required_any_of_attributes`, and `exclude_all_of_attributes` are all provided, an eligible vehicle must satisfy the following to be considered for assignments: 1. Meet all conditions specified in `required_all_of_attributes`. 2. Meet at least one of the conditions listed in `required_any_of_attributes`. 3. Not meet any conditions mentioned in `exclude_all_of_attributes`. Consequently, a vehicle which does not have any `attributes` defined can't be assigned to an order which has `vehicle_preferences` configured.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_all_of_attributes
description: An array of objects to add mandatory requirements for the order. A vehicle must **meet** **all conditions** specified here to be considered for assignment. Each object represents a single condition. Please note that a maximum of 10 conditions can be added here for a given order.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_all_of_attributes[].attribute
description: Specify the name of the attribute. The `attribute` is compared to the keys (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_all_of_attributes[].value
description: Specify the desired value of the attribute to be applied for this order. `value` provided here is compared to the values (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_all_of_attributes[].operator
description: Specify the operator to denote the relation between `attribute` and the `value` specified above. The `attribute` , `operator` and `value` together constitute the condition that a vehicle must meet to be eligible for assignment. Currently, we support following operators currently: * Equal to (==) * Less than (<) * Less tha equal to (<=) * Greater than (>) * Greater than equal to (>=) * Contains (contains) Please note that when using "contains" operator only one `value` can be specified and the corresponding `attribute` must contain multiple values when defined for a vehicle.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_any_of_attributes
description: An array of objects to add optional requirements for the order. A vehicle must **meet** **at least one of the conditions** specified here to be considered for assignment. Each object represents a single condition. Please note that a maximum of 10 conditions can be added here for a given order.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_any_of_attributes[].attribute
description: Specify the name of the attribute. The `attribute` is compared to the keys (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_any_of_attributes[].value
description: Specify the desired value of the attribute to be applied for this order. `value` provided here is compared to the values (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.required_any_of_attributes[].operator
description: Specify the operator to denote the relation between `attribute` and the `value` specified above. The `attribute` , `operator` and `value` together constitute the condition that a vehicle must meet to be eligible for assignment. Currently, we support following operators currently: * Equal to (==) * Less than (<) * Less tha equal to (<=) * Greater than (>) * Greater than equal to (>=) * Contains (contains) Please note that when using "contains" operator only one `value` can be specified and the corresponding `attribute` must contain multiple values when defined for a vehicle.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.exclude_all_of_attributes
description: An array of objects to add exclusion requirements for the order. A vehicle must **not meet any of the conditions** specified here to be considered for assignment. Each object represents a single condition. Please note that a maximum of 10 conditions can be added here for a given order.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.exclude_all_of_attributes[].attribute
description: Specify the name of the attribute. The `attribute` is compared to the keys (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.exclude_all_of_attributes[].value
description: Specify the desired value of the attribute to be applied for this order. `value` provided here is compared to the values (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: orders[].vehicle_preferences.exclude_all_of_attributes[].operator
description: Specify the operator to denote the relation between `attribute` and the `value` specified above. The `attribute` , `operator` and `value` together constitute the condition that a vehicle must meet to be eligible for assignment. Currently, we support following operators currently: * Equal to (==) * Less than (<) * Less tha equal to (<=) * Greater than (>) * Greater than equal to (>=) * Contains (contains) Please note that when using "contains" operator only one `value` can be specified and the corresponding `attribute` must contain multiple values when defined for a vehicle.

name: orders[].priority
description: Specify the priority for this order. A higher value indicates a higher priority. When specified, it will override any priority score deduced from `order_attribute_priority_mappings` for this order. Valid values are \[1, 10\] and default is 0.

name: orders[].attributes
description: Specify custom attributes for the orders. Each attribute should be created as a `key:value` pair. The **keys** provided can be used in `options.order_attribute_priority_mappings` to assign a custom priority for this order based on its attributes. The maximum number of key:value pairs that can be specified under `attributes` for a given order, is limited to 30.

name: vehicles
description: Collects the details of vehicles available to fulfill the orders. Each object represents one vehicle. All requests must include `vehicles` as a mandatory input. A maximum of 100 vehicles is allowed per request.

name: vehicles[].id
description: Specify a unique ID for the vehicle.

name: vehicles[].location
description: Specify the location coordinates where the vehicle is currently located. This input is mandatory for each vehicle.

name: vehicles[].location.lat
description: Latitude of the vehicle's current location.

name: vehicles[].location.lng
description: Longitude of the vehicle's current location.

name: vehicles[].attributes
description: Specify custom attributes for the vehicle. Each attribute should be created as a `key:value` pair. These attributes can be used in the `orders.vehicle_preferences` input to refine the search of vehicles for each order. The maximum number of key:value pairs that can be specified under `attributes` for a given vehicle, is limited to 30.

name: vehicles[].remaining_waypoints
description: An array of objects to collect the location coordinates of the stops remaining on an ongoing trip of the vehicle. The service can assign new orders to the vehicle if they are cost-effective. Once a new order is assigned, the vehicle must complete all the steps in the ongoing trip before proceeding to pickup the newly assigned order. Please note that a maximum of 10 waypoints can be specified for a given vehicle.

name: vehicles[].remaining_waypoints[].lat
description: Specify the latitude of the location.

name: vehicles[].remaining_waypoints[].lng
description: Specify the longitude of the location.

name: vehicles[].priority
description: Specify the priority for this vehicle. A higher value indicates a higher priority. When specified, it will override any priority score deduced from `vehicle_attribute_priority_mappings` for this vehicle. Valid values are \[1, 10\] and default is 0.

name: filter
description: Specify the filtering criterion for the vehicles with respect to each order's location. `filter` is a mandatory input for all requests.

name: filter.radius
description: Specify a radius, in meters, which will be used to filter out ineligible vehicles for each order. The pickup location of an order will act as the center of the circle when identifying eligible vehicles. Valid values for `radius` are \[1, 10000\].

name: filter.pickup_eta
description: Specify a duration, in seconds, which will be used to filter out ineligible vehicles for each order. Any vehicle which would take more time than specified here, to reach the pickup location of a given order, will be ruled out for assignment for that particular order. Valid values for `pickup_eta` are \[1, 3600\].

name: filter.driving_distance
description: Defines a `driving_distance` filter, in meters. If a vehicle needs to drive further than this distance to reach a pickup location, it will not be assigned to that order. Valid range of values for this filter is \[1, 10000\].

name: options
description: Configure the assignment constraints and response settings.

name: options.travel_cost
description: Choose a travel cost that will be used by the service for assigning vehicles efficiently from a set of qualifying ones.

name: options.dropoff_details
description: When **true**, the service returns the drop-off steps for each trip and related details in the response. Defaults to **false**.

name: options.order_attribute_priority_mappings
description: Collection of rules for assigning custom priority to orders based on their attributes. In case an order satisfies more than one rule, the highest priority score from all the rules satisfied, would be the effective priority score for such an order.

name: options.order_attribute_priority_mappings[].attribute
description: Specify the name of the attribute. The `attribute` is compared to the keys (of each `key:value` pair) in `orders.attributes` during evaluation.

name: options.order_attribute_priority_mappings[].value
description: Specify the desired value of the attribute to be applied for this order. `value` provided here is compared to the values (of each `key:value` pair) in `orders.attributes` during evaluation.

name: options.order_attribute_priority_mappings[].operator
description: Specify the operator to denote the relation between `attribute` and the `value` specified above. The `attribute` , `operator` and `value` together constitute the condition that an order must meet to assume the specified priority. We support the following operators currently: * Equal to (==) * Less than (<) * Less tha equal to (<=) * Greater than (>) * Greater than equal to (>=) * Contains (contains) Please note that when using "contains" operator only one `value` can be specified and the corresponding `attribute` must contain multiple values when defined for an order.

name: options.order_attribute_priority_mappings[].priority
description: Specify the priority score that should be assigned when an order qualifies the criteria specified above. A higher value indicates a higher priority. Valid values are \[1,10\].

name: options.vehicle_attribute_priority_mappings
description: Collection of rules for assigning custom priority to vehicles based on their attributes. In case a vehicle satisfies more than one rule, the highest priority score from all the rules satisfied, would be the effective priority score for such a vehicle.

name: options.vehicle_attribute_priority_mappings[].attribute
description: Specify the name of the attribute. The `attribute` is compared to the keys (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: options.vehicle_attribute_priority_mappings[].value
description: Specify the desired value of the attribute to be applied for this vehicle. `value` provided here is compared to the values (of each `key:value` pair) in `vehicles.attributes` during evaluation.

name: options.vehicle_attribute_priority_mappings[].operator
description: Specify the operator to denote the relation between `attribute` and the `value` specified above. The `attribute` , `operator` and `value` together constitute the condition that a vehicle must meet to assume the specified priority. We support the following operators currently: * Equal to (==) * Less than (<) * Less tha equal to (<=) * Greater than (>) * Greater than equal to (>=) * Contains (contains) Please note that when using "contains" operator only one `value` can be specified and the corresponding `attribute` must contain multiple values when defined for a vehicle.

name: options.vehicle_attribute_priority_mappings[].priority
description: Specify the priority score that should be assigned when a vehicle qualifies the criteria specified above. A higher value indicates a higher priority. Valid values are \[1,10\].

name: options.alternate_assignments
description: Specify the maximum number of potential, alternate vehicle assignments to be returned for each order, apart from the vehicle which was assigned as recommended. Please note that: * The maximum number of alternate assignments that can be requested are 3. * It is not necessary that the service will return the specified number of alternate assignments for each order. The number of alternate assignments returned will depend on the number of vehicles provided in the input. * Order which could not be assigned to any vehicles due to their `filter` or attribute matching criteria will not be eligible for alternate assignments as well.

name: options.routing
description: Specify routing preferences for route calculations and identifications.

name: options.routing.mode
description: Specify the traveling mode to be used for identifying routes, ETAs and distances.
